reviews.text: 大学的时候接触的盗版，当时一个宿舍玩的破解版联机很欢乐，现在看到了这个，准备补票然后在拉朋友一起继续浪。然后呢，MA的，汉化没有，我们找汉化，汉化黑屏我们继续解决，汉化解决连不了机我们还要解决，我想着不对啊，我特么买一个正版游戏这么折腾自己干嘛？下个破解版直接带汉化随便一个平台链接就能链接了，我特么跟个傻子一样在这里折腾正版，买个正版游戏还不如盗版方便？我也是服了，玩游戏是为了心情好，还没开完先折腾半小时跟神经病一样。
真的是正版游戏的受害者，7个小时的游戏体验，7个小时都在和朋友试联机，要不然就是游戏房间进不去，要不然就是高ping，还不如打个汉化补丁玩盗版，真的是，一般都不评论什么游戏，这个游戏真的是一绝

新手入门不要慌，官方中文记得装 开局一条大裤衩，装备手搓或搜刮 七天一波大尸潮，战士难度刚刚好 有朝一日钱在手，商店资源全带走 技能加点选专长，装备战力稳步涨 末日科学家崛起，机车飞机摆一起 跑酷连击全拉满，见人就抡王八拳 力量坚韧点一圈，铁王八蛋在人间 感知搜刮大法好，切格拉瓦满城跑 白天搜刮别太虎，晚上整理分清楚 搜刮同时把矿挖，优势地段建个家 跳楼撞头都很屌，另建新房挡尸潮 前期丧尸很辣鸡，点射爆头如杀鸡 晚上尽量不要浪，冲刺体力跟不上 多接任务多挖宝，多吃罐头身体好 同级装备看面板，模具记得要装满 民居门店搜书柜，技能不点我也会 近战弓弩枪与炮，技能加成很重要 生存思路提前想，乱点技能必抓狂 祖父秘方效果强，运用得当帮大忙 垃圾炮台不麻瓜，保护菊花好搜刮 电棒在手我张狂，我是教授我姓杨 弓弩记得装弓弦，准星不飘心不悬 手枪冲锋威力小，子弹堆叠却不少 神器AKM60，火力充足真无情 猎枪面板伤害棒，弹容一发有点伤 射手步枪也很强，百步穿杨小李广 雷筒双管泵动式，靠近一枪就去世 火箭手雷爆炸物，清尸潮中流砥柱 头盔护甲降移速，轻甲轻微重甲吐 噪音增加不友好，消音配件勤奋搞 不点驮骡做口袋，技能点是我最爱 改进消音净水器，头灯抗冲装甲板 此类配件优先凑，保暖隔热不用愁 四级务农农场主，三倍收获不吃土 我编不下去了

The game gets worse with each patch. When the community complains, the devs blame the community for them not being able to do more updates because they have to fix all the things they made worse. It's a cycle that's been going on for years and shows no signs of ever changing. The jar system they added (which was them attempting to save face after ruining a bunch of other survival aspects) sucks. It's just an annoyance that serves no real purpose. The smell system sucks. It "solved" a problem that didn't exist and just made managing food items even more of a chore for the player. The biome hazard system sucks. It feels the same in every biome - you get 3 minutes to be outside before you need to spend 1 minute inside. Eventually you craft an item become permanently immune to it. The storms that roll in are just more severe versions of this same mechanic. Ultimately it just wastes your time, as you need to keep afking inside structures to refill the meter. The items you can craft for temporary immunity only last 5 minutes and use difficult to acquire materials, making them largely useless. It's another problem that didn't need solving and just wastes your time. The central gameplay loop is getting a quest from a trader, which sends you to a nearby(ish) point of interest (POI), and then progressing through that POI to complete the objective. That typically involves either killing all zombies and/or fetching a special item. The POIs are really the best part of the game. There are a lot of them and many have really well done, under-stated story lines going on, e.g. a secret rooster fighting ring or animals being genetically altered. It's very much a "show, don't tell" approach that works well. Unfortunately, this is one of the only things I have to speak positively about. Stealth is mostly worthless now. They've moved more and more of the POI zombies to just appear out of thin air. Typically when they all spawn in, they immediately know where you are and charge straight at you. Quests at POIs typically require you to full clear the area to complete it, so there's really no avoiding these forced ambushes, even when you know exactly when and where they're coming from. Stealth against enemies that are spawned in normally generally works fine, but there are fewer and fewer spawned in that way. Some POI spawns are so badly set up that enemies will materialize just a few steps in front of you. Part of this was because they could never fix their performance issues from having more zombies spawned in. Had they made the spawns happen at more natural points (e.g. ascending to a second floor) they could've achieved more natural spawning without as much being in at once. Unfortunately, they did a half-assed job and now we just get things spawning in pre-aggroed all the time. Item progression sucks since 1.0. They nerfed quest rewards into the ground, so pretty much all of your armor and weapons come from crafting. The problem is they're all gated by the same materials. For example, a wooden bow, a compound bow, a crossbow, and a compound crossbow all require the same bow parts. All of them require the same legendary part for a tier 6. Because you can't make parts and they're found so rarely, you basically don't craft more than two of a weapon type throughout the whole game, with the second usually being a max level legendary. Since legendary parts for the best item type are the same as the worst item type, you're never going to make the lower type's legendary. Armor sets are worse than weapons. The only progression is tier 1 to tier 6 of a single armor type. Fortunately the set bonuses are mostly useless so you can just pick the individual item bonuses you want, but the system before sets was simply better. Do you really want to switch all your gear to a farmer set each time you harvest crops? Do you really want to switch all your gear to a mining set each time you mine ore? Do you really want to switch all your gear to a lumberjack set each time you chop wood? It's just more player time wasted. The current map generation sucks. The one good thing is that the actual generation time is much faster -- it used to take as much as 15 minutes to complete. However, they changed how biome are laid out and now they look completely artificial. The default, center forest, makes the middle circle of the map a forest and each remaining corner a different biome. There's no more natural transitions between biomes. The other options you can choose from are worse. When they changed the map generation, they also made forest settlements tiny. You only get only small towns, which means a low number of POIs. This cannot be controlled in the generation config. This very rapidly leads to the first trader sending you to POIs 1km+ away, as early as the first day or two. This is a huge waste of player time as that takes a long time to travel on a bike, let alone on food. Imagine doing 30 quests where half of them involve spending 5 minutes just traveling to the POI. That's the current state. The one good? thing about this game is all the old major versions are selectable from the config. But, if your selling point is "just play the version from 5 years ago," it's not very compelling. 7 Days has been in development for 13 years, and 2 years have passed since 1.0 was released along with paid cosmetic DLCs (which, incidentally, were part of the onus for changing the armor and clothing system since they needed a way to shoehorn them in). The game is now all the way up to 3.0, but for some reason they're still calling it early access. Overall there's just not much reason to start playing now as a new player, since you can just expect the game to continue in the downward trajectory it's been on for years.

I've been playing for over 10 years. I've watched it evolve over the years into what it is now, looking forward to every Alpha as if it were a new game release. Many people complain about the fact that it's never finished but honestly that's what I love about it. It's always growing and adapting. There is always something new. The devs listen to feedback and try to give the players whatever experience they want. For $10 10 years ago I've had the joy of playing many many different games within one. This game is akin to my Minecraft experience. As in you don't play for some epic storyline (story is non existent) or even the great gameplay (balance and pacing is questionable), but due to the creative freedom you have over the world. Turn any building into an zombie deathtrap or deconstruct anything in the world for resources. There is something to be said for a game that lets you build miles of underground tunnels that you can travel from base to base with on a motorcycle. I have 1,000's of hours in this game, mostly in mods, and restarting from scratch every time I die. I don't regret any of it. My only real gripe is the games development. The main game, outside the mods, really hasn't been advancing in a meaningfully forward direction. Features are added, taken away, *improved* or downgraded with every patch. It is a much different game from when it was in early access, but I don't think it necessarily a better game? It changed from an open world to a place where all houses and buildings become mini-dungeons with their own loot rooms at the end. It moved from open survival to running Trader Quests over and over again. You technically have the option to "Play the game your way", but why do that when the optimal way to play is handed to you? I feel as if the game had so much potential to be even more than it is, and I hope that the developers keep moving on the path of improvement rather than continuing change for change's sake. Until then, the mod community provides. Overall though, there isn't a game quite like 7dtd. It's gamey enough that it doesn't quite slog along like project zomboid, but also sandbox enough that one can do whatever they want creatively to the world. The early game is fun, and I think you would do well to stretch it out as long as possible. Late game, zombies will barely challenge you on anything but the highest difficulties and then only because they're bullet sponges. I sense people, including myself, will be playing this one for a long time.

Once upon a time there was a wonderful zombie game. The graphics weren't stellar, the gameplay was a bit janky, and you died to zombies a lot. But this game had a wonderful charm to it, You and your friends would chop trees, mine rock, farm, kill zombies and hunt animals for food. You scavenged clothes like flannel shirts, and parkas so you could survive the frozen areas, and looked for hats and drinks so you could survive the heat of the desert. All the while, the skills you used most would go up, and people ended up specialized in areas like fighting, building, farming, etc. All the while, you desperately gathered resources, and weapons to survive the dreaded Horde Night, Over time, your Horde Base got stronger, and more defensible, your weapons got better, and the Hordes got larger, but a well designed, and put together base made it easier to survive the Night. Then one day, the developers stopped seeing the players as the customers of their game, or people who were enjoying their product, and started seeing them as the enemy who were "Not playing our game right." Everytime the players came up with a clever way design a base to fight zombies, they took it as an insult to their ego, and changed the game to negate whatever tactic the players had figured out. Then, they decided that the game was too 'open world' and put magic force fields to prevent players from entering biomes that they devs felt the players hadn't earned... from doing quests... in a ZOMBIE APOCALYPSE. My friends and I have over 2000 hours in this game, but no more. The devs won, they beat all the fun out of the game. Avoid at all costs.

Yes, on sale for the original starting price of $25, I can definitely recommend this. It took over a decade, but now the game is at a point where you can play it reliably, and most importantly for a zombie sandbox, in your own style. You can tweak the sandbox settings to your liking and that is the biggest thing I've seen added in the lifespan of this game. When I had the original release, there was a real charm to the natural elements survival that this game had. It was man vs. nature... zombies were feral at best, but a constant threat. And because there weren't any man-made landmarks to use to your advantage, you had to build you fortress from the ground up. Then all the extra enemies and biomes and blood moon and stuff started getting added. While I appreciate these mechanics and see their purpose, it muddled the survival experience in to something of a tower defense experience. Your first priority became finding a reinforceable position, often a multi-story building, because you had no choice but to adhere to these new threats. Fast-forward to now, and you're able to control very minute details of the survival experience. I promptly created a Project-Zomboid like experience where the zombies can only walk, only spawn standard, and bonus, so I can learn all the new crafting-trees without going to the meta, increase spawn rates and other options. Anyone familiar with Project Zomboid will see the customization options closely match what they have for sandbox options. This is REALLY GREAT. It's not like I don't see the fun in playing it their way, but just like PZ, I found happiness when I was able to adjust the experience to my liking. For anyone looking for a great zombie survival-crafting sandbox game, I would say this is almost a better choice than Project Zomboid. I put over 1000 hours in to that game, also purchased early in it's development cycle, and unfortunately this 7 Days To Die, finally with the sandbox settings, has won the race by my measure.

虽然游戏时间只有1000+小时，但确实感受到制作组的辛苦与用心，浅谈一下个人游戏感受，本次的3.0大版本更新确实开放太多的自定义参数，同时满足了98%玩家体验；官方给出的固定模式也很大程度上的迎合了许多玩家。其实可以看出来，制作组很努力的想要现实化末日游戏的场景，对于土匪系统，我感觉没有必要死磕怎么还不上，就像现在的AI，不管你怎么弄依然还是会有玩家利用各种算法将它们变的呆傻。当然这也是游戏的另一种玩法。无可厚非土匪出来也将变为下一个跳尸桥的产物。我更倾向于末日孤独生存。现如今的风暴系统算是弥补了我当时初次体验的想法，会有酸雨，雷暴的极端恶劣天气，不妨在添加一些超低温度和高温的缺失，我说的是全地图冰河期或是高温期。这些极端天气对玩家的伤害不同，酸雨和雷暴腐蚀或摧毁玩家所在的建筑方块或是装备，同时疾病也可以伴随出现。还有农作物的疾病都会大大增加玩家的生存难度。极端天气和血月的同时出现想想都刺激与折磨，毕竟谁也没有经历过末世，哪我们不妨在大胆一些，超级僵尸作为21天或28天的小BOSS应该也不错，现在的强力僵尸，好像真的不太强力。其次是任务会导致僵尸被标记，当然是防止玩家遗漏导致任务失败，只标记最后3只更合适，危险处处都在才是制作组的核心吧。还有僵尸的复活和假死状态也是不错的选择。个人接受不了的是手搓直升机！！！汽车，摩托，感觉这些还说的过去，直升机就很难共情，当然不排除末世存活下的厉害工程师，适当提高一下手搓直升机的难度。或者单独出杂志降低杂志出现的概率。总之这是一个不错的游戏，感谢制作团队的付出。值得大家去创造和体验自己的末世生存。
